commit_message:
Add constant evaluation support for the `struct.new[_default]` Wasm GC instructions (#9282)

* Add constant evaluation support for the `struct.new[_default]` Wasm GC instructions

* fix no-gc builds

* wrap const evaluation in `AutoAssertNoGc`

* add assertions that we access `VMGcRef`s in native-endian

* fix an endian mismatch bug between compiled wasm code and host code

fix_commit_message:
Don't unwrap results of const-eval (#11557)

While all const expressions executed at runtime are valid they can still
fail due to GC OOM or failure to allocate more GC memory. As a result
all `unwrap()` on `eval(...)` is removed in favor of propagating
upwards the result.

Closes #11469
agent_reasoning: The struct.new/struct.new_default const-eval support added a fallible GC allocation path into `ConstExprEvaluator::eval`. The pre-existing global-initialization caller (`Instance::initialize_vmctx_globals`) was written before that allocation could fail, so it called `.expect("should be a valid const expr")` on the result, treating any evaluation failure as proof of an invalid module. A guest module with a struct-typed global initializer can legitimately hit this path and fail due to GC OOM/allocation failure at instantiation time, which would turn a recoverable condition into a host-side panic (embedder DoS). The fix changes `initialize_vmctx_globals` to return `Result<()>` and propagate the error with `?`, and wires that fallible call into the existing fallible instance post-initialization step so the error surfaces as a normal instantiation `Result::Err` instead of aborting the process.
